title: Open means dark
description: One break anywhere on a series loop stops the flow. The lamp goes dark even if every part is still on the table.

blocks.md:
## One gap is enough

On a series loop, current is all or nothing. Close the path and a current can exist. Open one gap — a switch, a loose clip, a dead cell — and the current is zero. The lamp goes dark even if the battery is strong and the bulb is new.

This bites when you hunt for a “weak lamp” and ignore the gap. Nearby parts are not a circuit. The picture with the dashed break is the whole lesson.

![An open gap keeps the lamp dark](assets/open-loop.svg)

```text
battery → resistor →  GAP  → lamp   (dark)
```

A common mistake is thinking a tiny gap still leaks a little light. In these lessons an open path is I = 0. The questions ask you to read the open picture, then say why the lamp is dark.

blocks.promptMd: Tap the gap that keeps this lamp dark.
blocks.explainMd: The dashed red break in the loop is the open point. That is why the lamp cannot light.

blocks.promptMd: If the battery and the lamp are both on the table, the lamp can glow even with a gap in the wire.
blocks.explainMd: On the table is not a loop. An open path is dark.

blocks.promptMd: The lamp is dark. The most useful first question is…

choices.md: Is the path closed all the way around?
Should I add more cells first?
An open loop can still leak a little light

blocks.explainMd: Find the break before you blame the battery or the bulb.
